findings.title: H427-SCALE: Verified counterexample to the stated general-preconditioner extension
source_locators: Theorem 6.10, p.29; dependency on Theorem 6.1(D), Fact 6.9, and (6.4)

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.claim_location: Theorem 6.10, p.29; dependency on Theorem 6.1(D), Fact 6.9, and (6.4)
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.status: Verified counterexample to the stated general-preconditioner extension
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.severity_suggestion: Major for the extension; primary assigns final severity and numbering
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.exact_setup: For p>=3 let u=2^{-p}, m=2,n=1, A=b=(1,0)^T, x=1, kappa(A)=1, Rhat=u, xhat0=1+2u. Let the inner routine be g(c)=u*c, equivalently one Richardson step from zero with step u for this scalar system. M=Rhat^{-T}A^T A Rhat^{-1}=u^{-2}.

hypotheses_checked.A: kappa*u=u tends to zero at fixed m,n.
hypotheses_checked.C_prime: Rhat is triangular and nonsingular; cond(A Rhat^{-1})=1. Fact 6.9 holds with ||A(x-xhat0)||=2u, while ||b-Ax||+||x||u=u, so its hidden constant can be 2.
hypotheses_checked.D: For every scalar c, |g(c)-M^{-1}c|=u(1-u)|c|<=kappa*u*|c|. Multiplication by the power of two u is exact in the no-over/underflow model used for the example.
hypotheses_checked.B: Both xhat1 and xhat2 obey the output lower bound up to constants independent of u: |xhat1|>=0.5*(1+u) and xhat2>=1+u. Thus the final nonpathological assumption is satisfied.
hypotheses_checked.roundoff: The reviewer script checks every operation against nearest-even binary p-bit rounding and |delta|<=u. First-step operations are exact; only the final second-step addition in the displayed family requires rounding.

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.first_step: r0=-2u, c0=-2, dy0=-2u, dx0=-2, xhat1=-1+2u. Hence |xhat1-x|=2-2u, not O(u).
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.second_step: r1=2-2u, c1=2/u-2, dy1=2-2u, dx1=2/u-2. The exact sum is 2/u-3+2u; nearest p-bit rounding gives xhat2=2/u-2.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.backward_error: If both ||Delta A|| and ||Delta b|| are <=epsilon<1, the solution magnitude is <=(1+epsilon)/(1-epsilon). For X=xhat2>1 the least common perturbation bound is epsilon=(X-1)/(X+1), attained by Atilde=(1-epsilon)e1 and btilde=(1+epsilon)e1. It tends to 1, so X is not backward stable.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.local_checks: Exact p-bit simulations for p=10,20,40,53 and an actual native binary64 p=53 calculation all pass the stated identities and standard-roundoff checks. These finite checks support the analytic family; they are not presented as exhaustive formal proof checking.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.cause: Bounded cond(ARhat^{-1}) does not control its scale. Reusing the unscaled inner-error condition (6.2) admits an error that is amplified by Rhat^{-1}. Several uses of Lemma 6.3 cannot be recovered from condition number alone.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.proposed_correction: Add uniform two-sided absolute singular-value bounds on ARhat^{-1}, as supplied by the sketch-QR construction, or formulate and prove a scale-aware alternative inner-accuracy hypothesis.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.counterevidence_and_scope: The construction violates the absolute normalization of Lemma 6.3. It does not refute Theorem 6.1 with sketch-QR normalization, Theorem 7.1's correctly specified main FOSSILS method, or the corresponding normalized SPIR mechanism.

findings.severity_reason: An explicit family satisfies all stated assumptions of Theorem6.10 and disproves both asserted stability conclusions at fixed dimension. Scale correction changes the hypothesis.

findings.title: H427-ALG4: Actual typeset discrepancies confirmed; retained code provides scope-limiting counterevidence

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.status: Actual typeset discrepancies confirmed; retained code provides scope-limiting counterevidence
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.severity_suggestion: A grouped substantive algorithm-correction finding; primary sets final severity and count

components.issue: d=12n followed by beta=d/n gives beta=12 and alpha=(1-beta)^2=121, reversing the intended ratio.
components.decisive_check: The scalar homogeneous error recurrence has characteristic-root product beta=12, hence spectral radius >1. For M=3/2,c=1 with both initial iterates 1, its first update is -119/2 instead of exact solution 2/3. Correct beta=1/12 gives alpha=121/144 and first update 167/288; the corrected characteristic roots have modulus sqrt(1/12)<1.
components.counterevidence: Algorithm 2 / formula (2.10) use beta=eta^2. Retained fossils.m line 32 uses size(c,1)/d, equal to n/d at full rank.

components.issue: d initially holds the column-norm vector, then is overwritten by the scalar sketch dimension; the final diag(d)^{-1} therefore no longer restores column scaling.
components.decisive_check: Even if all inner solves are correct, the n=1 column-norm-2 case with normalized solution 2 must unscale to 1; overwritten d=12 instead gives 1/6 under the scalar interpretation. For n>1 the scalar/vector conflict is also a dimensional ambiguity.
components.counterevidence: Retained metasolver.m keeps scale=vecnorm(A) and returns x./scale.'.

components.issue: The condition i=1 and MOD(i,5)=0 uses outer i in {0,1}, so the intended second-refinement adaptive test never runs.
components.decisive_check: Direct finite evaluation of both allowed outer values gives false for the condition; the inner j does not occur in the printed test.
components.counterevidence: Retained metasolver.m uses loop==2 and mod(i,5)==0, where i is the inner iteration index.

components.issue: The printed +mu^2 z uses an undefined mu and adds the n-dimensional z outside P^T even after rank truncation; a regularized normal-operator term would require the corresponding projected, scaled term with the sign induced by c-Mdy.
components.decisive_check: After truncation P is n by r and delta y,c are r-dimensional while z=P delta y is n-dimensional. The displayed addition is not dimensionally valid for r<n.
components.counterevidence: Retained code forms the regularized residual right-hand side, and RAAR applies V'*(A^T A z+reg^2 z) divided by sreg; fossils.m subtracts this normal operator in c-Ady.

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.important_caveat: For M=1 and y0=y1=c the initial error is exactly zero; instability of the homogeneous recurrence alone then needs a perturbation. The M=3/2 initialized example avoids this caveat.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.scope: These findings concern printed recommended pseudocode. Static retained code inspection is counterevidence against alleging that the published implementation uses those defective steps. No author software was executed.

findings.severity_reason: Printed recommended algorithm reverses a contractionparameter and loses outputscaling, withadditionalunusablebranches. Retainedcodecounterevidence limitsattributiontothespecification.

findings.title: H427-C40: Verified false numerical inference; qualitative output theorem not disproved
source_locators: Theorem 8.2 proof, p.35, invoking Fact 8.1 on p.34

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.claim_location: Theorem 8.2 proof, p.35, invoking Fact 8.1 on p.34
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.status: Verified false numerical inference; qualitative output theorem not disproved
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.exact_example: Let eta=7/8, A=[I_n;0], and SA=diag(1/8,15/8,1,...,1). Take d=n and n sufficiently large for the logarithmic-dimension hypothesis. This is an allowed embedding with kappa(A)=1. Exact QR gives normal-matrix extreme eigenvalues 64 and 64/225, hence cond(M)=225>40.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.cause: From eta<=0.9, the generic exact bound is ((1+eta)/(1-eta))^2<=361, with small perturbation allowance needed in floating point; 40 does not follow.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.counterevidence_and_repair: The default eta=1/2 gives a bound 9. A fixed larger condition cap and a corresponding adjusted fixed approximation interval in Appendix C can preserve the qualitative logarithmic iteration estimate. The example does not show unstable SPIR output.

findings.severity_reason: False condition40 inference at allowedeta, but fixedconditioncapandapproximationintervalcanberepairedwithoutchangingqualitativetheorem; nofalseSPIRoutputestablished.

findings.title: H427-ZERO: Verified omitted zero-right-hand-side boundary guard in printed Lanczos routine

decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.status: Verified omitted zero-right-hand-side boundary guard in printed Lanczos routine
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.evidence: The routine sets gamma=||c|| and q1=c/gamma without first handling c=0; the later beta_{i+1}=0 check occurs after this undefined division.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.attainable_case: An exact consistent sketch-and-solve start can have xhat0=x and hence c0=Rhat^{-T}A^T(b-Axhat0)=0. For example, A=[I_n;0], b=A e1 and an exact isometric sketch on its range suffice.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.correction: Return the zero inner solution immediately when c=0.
decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence.scope: This is a printed-routine boundary omission. No claim is made about an uninspected author Lanczos implementation.

findings.severity_reason: Local zero-input normalization boundary guard, with exact zero solution immediate. Nonzero-input Lanczos proof unaffected; no uninspectedimplementationclaim.

additional_local_corrections_not_counted.limit: The loose final inequality may still hold. No independent defect count or false-output-bound claim follows from this identity alone.

additional_local_corrections_not_counted.correction: The printed bounds/monotonicity statements involving j(1.01)^{j-1} omit eta; the intended contracting expression includes 1.01*eta.
additional_local_corrections_not_counted.limit: No counterexample to the final theorem is asserted from these obvious local transcription issues.
